questions.question: The negation of "It is raining and it is cold" is
options: It is not raining and it is not cold
It is not raining or it is not cold
It is raining or it is cold
It is raining and it is not cold
questions.explanation: By De Morgan's law: not (P and Q) = not P or not Q.

questions.question: The negation of "All birds can fly" is
questions.explanation: The negation of "All" is "Some … not".

questions.question: If P then Q is true and P is true. Then
options: Nothing can be said about Q
questions.explanation: Modus ponens: from P → Q and P we get Q.

questions.question: If it rains, the match is cancelled. The match was not cancelled. We can conclude
options: The match was played in the rain
questions.explanation: Contrapositive: if not cancelled, then it did not rain.

questions.question: Ravi is tall or fast. Ravi is not tall. Then
questions.explanation: The "or" statement requires at least one true; since not tall, he is fast.

questions.question: The statement "P and Q" is true only when
options: both P and Q are true
questions.explanation: A conjunction needs both parts true.

questions.question: The contrapositive of "If x is even, then x² is even" is
options: If x² is not even, then x is not even
If x² is even, then x is even
If x is not even, then x² is not even
If x is even, then x² is not even
questions.explanation: Contrapositive: If not Q then not P.

questions.question: "I will go only if it does not rain" means
options: If it does not rain, I will go
If I do not go, it rains
I will go if it rains
If I go, then it does not rain
questions.explanation: "P only if Q" means If P then Q.

questions.question: "Unless you study, you will fail" is equivalent to
options: If you study, you will fail
If you fail, you did not study
If you study, you will pass
If you do not study, you will fail
questions.explanation: "Unless P, Q" means If not P then Q.

questions.question: The negation of "Some students are absent" is
questions.explanation: The negation of "Some" is "No".

questions.question: If A then B, and if B then C. Which follows?
options: If not A then not C
questions.explanation: The chain rule: A → B and B → C give A → C.

questions.question: The converse of "If it is a square, it is a rectangle" is
options: If it is a rectangle, it is a square
If it is not a square, it is not a rectangle
If it is not a rectangle, it is not a square
It is a square and a rectangle
questions.explanation: The converse swaps the two parts: If Q then P. It is not necessarily true.

questions.question: The statement "If 2 + 2 = 5, then the moon is made of cheese" is
questions.explanation: A conditional with a false antecedent is true.

questions.question: "Either P or Q but not both" is true when
options: P and Q are both true
P and Q are both false
neither P nor Q is true
P is true and Q is false
questions.explanation: Exclusive or is true when exactly one is true.

questions.question: If it rains, the ground is wet. The ground is wet. Therefore it rained. This reasoning is
questions.explanation: The ground may be wet for another reason. Q does not imply P.

questions.question: The negation of "If P then Q" is
options: If not P then not Q
questions.explanation: A conditional is false only when P is true and Q is false.

questions.question: A is true only if B is true. B is false. Then
options: A may be true or false
questions.explanation: A → B and not B give not A.

questions.question: "Neither Ravi nor Meena passed" means
options: Ravi did not pass and Meena did not pass
Ravi did not pass or Meena did not pass
questions.explanation: Neither means both failed.

questions.question: All who study pass. Anil did not pass. Therefore
options: Everyone who did not study failed
questions.explanation: Contrapositive: if not pass, then not study.

questions.question: Given P → Q, (not Q) or R, and P is true. Then
options: Nothing can be said about R
questions.explanation: From P → Q and P, Q is true. Then "not Q or R" with Q true forces R true.
